newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rallies as offshore players sell dollar.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rallies as offshore players sell dollar.

text.p: Thai baht rallied in late trade on Monday as foreign players unloaded long dollar positions to raise short-term baht funds, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 25.650/25.750 to the dollar late, against 25.810/25.850 in early morning trade, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.78 per dollar against 25.82 on Friday.
"Offshore players are unwinding their long dollar positions. It was very expensive for them to raise baht in the swap market," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Dealers said the Bank of Thailand still maintained its request for Thai banks not to quote short-term baht/dollar deals for offshore parties and the measure was effective in blocking speculators from raising baht in the spot market to bet against the baht.

The central bank on Friday made it clear that foreign speculators who earlier sold the baht heavily for dollars would have to pay a high price when they bought back firmer baht to square their positions.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium soared to 70/100 satangs/dollar in late trade from 30/50 in the early morning.
"Most offshore players attempted to push the swap rate up among themselves. There was nothing to worry about," said one swap market dealer.
Higher liquidity eased the overnight interbank rate to 13.00-15.00 percent late from 15.00-16.00 in the early morning.
